messages:
ryan: deploy-bot blocked the staging->canary publish for billing-worker. registry returned 'retag-conflict' and provenance mismatch across mirrors. bot log below. looking for a quick decision: fast-forward retag, pin, or shadow canary?

deploy-bot: publish blocked (code 409).
  image: public.ecr.aws/redwood/billing-worker:staging-canary-20260325
  reason: retag-conflict (target digest exists with different provenance) + mirror-provenance-drift (gcr vs ecr)
  note: existing digest public.ecr.aws/redwood/billing-worker@sha256:91a7... has cosign.attestations.kms=false upstream; our new build has kms=true -> registry rejects retag
  suggested_actions: [pin-prev-digest, republish-with-consistent-annot, shadow-canary-with-sidecar]

kim: what was the source of the mismatch? did builder flip the kms flag?

sasha: build metadata shows `--annotate kms=true` for this run. upstream test mirror shows previous canary had kms=false (historical). replication change last month may have allowed annotation differences.

ryan: we can't retag over an existing digest that has a different provenance policy. options:
- pin-prev-digest: unblock window quickly, no user impact, then plan a republish in maintenance window;
- republish-and-overwrite: build+push new digest and attempt to replace (risky, may be rejected by registry policy);
- shadow-canary: push a separate shadow image (staging-canary-shadow-20260325) and run tests side-by-side without shifting traffic. buys time for audit but increases complexity.

ops-bot: note: registry policy prohibits overwriting digests with different provenance metadata unless admin override is used. Admin override requires two approvers.

kim: I'd avoid admin override. Shadow canary seems safer if we want to exercise the new binary now, but it means we won't test the normal canary path. If we need to validate behavior on production-like path, pinning is better.

sasha: quick risk matrix: pin = lowest customer risk, delays provenance remediation; shadow = medium risk (test binary but not registry path), republish = higher risk operationally.

ryan: leaning pin + scheduled republish. We need a clear audit trail explaining why hash mismatch happened and a patch to publisher to check mirror annotations before finalize. Also need to update release notes.

deploy-bot: executing pin-prev-digest -> pinned public.ecr.aws/redwood/billing-worker@sha256:91a7... (previous canary digest). rollback-block cleared.

kim: creating follow-up ticket RE-4722: "billing-worker: reconcile provenance mismatch + republish plan". Tasks: (1) run `skopeo inspect --raw` against src and mirror to capture annotation diff; (2) validate cosign key on builders; (3) add preflight `cosign verify-attestation` and fail early; (4) test shadow canary process and document runbook; (5) schedule republish in 03:00-05:00 UTC window.

sasha: I'll take (1) and (3). Adding `--dry-run` for shadow canary to the ticket so teams can opt-in during emergency.

ryan: release notes snippet: "Canary held: provenance metadata mismatch between mirror and build prevented retag; pinned to previous digest (sha256:91a7...); remediation RE-4722 scheduled during maintenance window."

kim: pinging support and security for audit entry. Also flagging replication team to review mirror config.

ops-bot: RE-4722 created and assigned. Please add logs and skopeo output to the ticket.

ryan: thanks all. leaving thread open until RE-4722 has the preflight merged. If anyone needs to attempt a shadow canary now, reply here with justification. :eyes:
